problem_contract.description: Read two signed 32-bit integers separated by whitespace and print their mathematical sum followed by a newline.
problem_contract.output_rule: The sum must be printed exactly as a signed 64-bit decimal integer.

structure.scoring_note: Configured deterministic severity deductions; findings are not proof of exploitability.

modularity.measurement_note: Lizard-based cyclomatic complexity and per-function NLOC.

complexity.measurement_note: Lizard-based cyclomatic complexity and per-function NLOC.

results.description: Large sum still within signed 32-bit range

logical.score_basis: fraction of configured edge/corner cases passed

runtime_efficiency.measurement_note: Wall time includes Docker exec overhead; use for relative grading in the same environment, not as isolated CPU time.

usefulness.example: An instructor evaluates a class set of C submissions against the same versioned rules and hidden tests, then reviews the failing inputs and per-metric evidence.
usefulness.benefit: Reduces repetitive compile-and-test work while keeping grades reproducible from the source hash and rules hash.

usefulness.example: A student submits a program before the deadline and receives exact failing inputs, expected outputs, compiler diagnostics, and bounded runtime findings.
usefulness.benefit: Helps students reproduce and fix defects before manual assessment.

usefulness.example: A course uses Valgrind, ASan/UBSan, static diagnostics, and source review to prioritize submissions that need a closer manual check.
usefulness.benefit: Combines independent runtime and source-level signals instead of relying on output correctness alone.

usefulness.use_case: Similarity triage across a course corpus
usefulness.example: With an instructor-authorized corpus populated, the similarity analyzer flags submissions whose token-shingle overlap exceeds the configured threshold.
usefulness.benefit: Narrows the set of submissions an instructor needs to inspect; it does not determine plagiarism or authorship.

limitations.example: A sum program passes every supplied case but receives 2147483647 and 1 when no overflow case is configured; the program may invoke signed integer overflow.
limitations.mitigation: Define the numeric contract in rules, include boundary/counterexample tests, and state exactly which inputs were exercised.

limitations.limitation: Dynamic tools only observe executed paths
limitations.example: A memory leak occurs only after a rare error branch; if none of the configured tests enters that branch, Valgrind may report a clean run.
limitations.mitigation: Expand tests to exercise error paths and retain source-level review as a complementary, non-conclusive signal.

limitations.limitation: Heuristic and LLM judgments can be subjective
limitations.example: A short, clear program uses single-letter loop indices; a style heuristic may penalize it even when the instructor rubric does not require longer names or comments.
limitations.mitigation: Keep the instructor rubric authoritative, classify non-rubric suggestions as optional, and require evidence IDs for factual claims.

limitations.limitation: Similarity is not proof of copying or LLM use
limitations.example: Two students independently write the same short scanf/printf solution and exceed a similarity threshold because the task has very little possible code structure.
limitations.mitigation: Use similarity only to flag candidates for instructor review; compare distinctive logic and context before drawing conclusions.
